subject: Operations
title: Single vs. Multi-Sourcing
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Single vs. Multi-Sourcing.

hook.text: Apple relied on one factory for a critical chip. An earthquake hit. Millions of iPhones were delayed.

buildup.text: Single sourcing means one supplier per component—simpler management but higher risk if that supplier fails.

discovery.text: Multi-sourcing spreads risk across suppliers but increases complexity, coordination effort, and sometimes cost.

twist.text: Dual sourcing is a middle ground—two suppliers for critical items, single source for non-critical ones.

climax.text: After COVID, companies shifted critical components to dual or regional sourcing to reduce concentration risk.

punchline.text: One supplier is simple. Two is safe. Choose wisely.

quiz.question: What is the main risk of single sourcing?
